rationale: Initial molecular discovery in 2018 (Source [8], DOI: 10.1038/s41588-018-0042-y) demonstrated that while BRD4 haploinsufficiency produces an atypical CdLS phenotype, a specific de novo missense variant impairing histone acetyl-lysine recognition while retaining NIPBL interaction caused a more typical CdLS presentation. However, subsequent larger cohort and review studies (Jouret et al. 2022; Lonardo et al. 2025; Kaur et al. 2023) show that BRD4 alterations overall—both truncating and missense variants—underlie non-classic, atypical CdLS or a distinct BRD4-related neurodevelopmental disorder recognizable and distinguishable from classic NIPBL-driven CdLS. Kaur et al. 2023 specifically note that NIPBL remains the only gene definitively associated with classic/severe CdLS, placing BRD4 among non-classic disorder of transcriptional regulation (DTR) genes. Thus, while the biochemical mechanism is experimentally validated, the claim that BRD4 missense variants produce a true classical CdLS presentation remains conflicted with broader clinical cohort delineations.

evidence.text: BRD4 haploinsufficiency was found to cause a phenotype overlapping with atypical CdLS, whereas a de novo missense variant preserving NIPBL interaction but disrupting acetylated histone binding resulted in a more typical CdLS clinical presentation.

source.title: Cornelia de Lange syndrome: from molecular diagnosis to ...
source.quote: We found that the clinical phenotype associated with BRD4 haploinsufficiency overlapped with that of Cornelia de Lange syndrome (CdLS), which is most often caused by mutation of NIPBL. More typical CdLS was observed with a de novo BRD4 missense variant, which retained the ability to coimmunoprecipitate with NIPBL, but bound poorly to acetylated histones.

evidence.text: BRD4 pathogenic variants, including both premature truncating and missense variants, are comprehensively classified as causative factors for non-classic, milder, or atypical forms of CdLS rather than classic CdLS.

source.title: Non-Classic Cornelia de Lange Syndrome Due to BRD4 Gene Alterations: A Literature Review
source.quote: Pathogenic variations in the NIPBL gene account for the majority of cases, but variations in several other genes, including BRD4, have been identified as causative factors for non-classic or milder forms of the syndrome. This review aims to analyse the roles that BRD4 plays in the various pathways in which it is involved and to summarise current knowledge on atypical CdLS associated with BRD4 gene alterations

evidence.text: An international cohort study of 14 new patients delineated BRD4-related disorder as a clinically recognizable syndrome distinguishable from classic Cornelia de Lange syndrome and other cohesinopathies.

source.title: Understanding the new BRD4‐related syndrome: Clinical and genomic delineation with an international cohort study
source.quote: We report the first cohort of patients with BRD4-related disorder and delineate the dysmorphic features at different ages. This work extends the phenotypic spectrum of cohesinopathies and characterize a new clinically relevant and recognizable pattern, distinguishable from the other cohesinopathies.

evidence.text: Comprehensive analysis across 716 probands demonstrates that NIPBL is the only gene identified that results in classic or severe CdLS, whereas causative variants in BRD4 result in a non-classic CdLS-like phenotype within disorders of transcriptional regulation.

source.title: Genomic analyses in Cornelia de Lange Syndrome and related diagnoses: Novel candidate genes, genotype–phenotype correlations and common mechanisms
source.journal: American Journal of Medical Genetics Part A
source.quote: NIPBL accounting for the majority (>60%) of cases, and the only gene identified to date that results in the severe or classic form of CdLS when mutated. Pathogenic variants in cohesin genes other than NIPBL tend to result in a less severe phenotype. Causative variants in additional genes, such as ANKRD11, EP300, AFF4, TAF1, and BRD4, can cause a CdLS-like phenotype.

evidence.text: NIPBL directly interacts with BRD4 through its extra-terminal (ET) domain and cooperates in transcriptional regulation at co-occupied super-enhancers and promoters, explaining molecular overlap between CdLS and BRD4 mutations.

source.title: The Cornelia de Lange Syndrome-associated factor NIPBL ...
source.quote: Thus, we provide evidence for NIPBL and BRD4 cooperation in transcriptional regulation, which should contribute to explain the recently observed CdLS-like phenotype associated with BRD4 mutations.

conflicts: Olley et al. (Nat Genet 2018 / Sarogni 2020) reported that a de novo missense variant in BRD4 causing disrupted histone acetylation binding while retaining NIPBL interaction produced a 'more typical CdLS' phenotype compared to truncating loss-of-function variants.

Subsequent cohort analyses and consensus reviews (Jouret et al. 2022, Kaur et al. 2023, Lonardo et al. 2025) conclude that NIPBL is the only gene that causes classic/severe CdLS, and that BRD4 alterations—including missense variants—cause an atypical, non-classic CdLS or a distinct BRD4-related syndrome distinguishable from classic CdLS.

new_directions.question_text: Does systematic CdLS consensus scoring (Kline et al. criteria) quantitatively differentiate BD1/BD2 bromodomain missense variants from truncating BRD4 variants across all pooled international cases?
new_directions.rationale: Initial studies described bromodomain missense cases as 'more typical CdLS' based on qualitative gestalt, but systematic application of the international CdLS clinical consensus score is required to objectively test whether they meet formal criteria for classic CdLS.

new_directions.question_text: Do specific missense variants in the extra-terminal (ET) domain of BRD4 disrupting direct NIPBL binding cause a distinct clinical presentation compared to bromodomain acetylation-binding pocket variants?
new_directions.rationale: Because BRD4 interacts with NIPBL via its ET domain while binding chromatin via bromodomains, dissecting domain-specific missense alleles will clarify the exact molecular pathophysiology governing the phenotypic spectrum.
